subproblem.title: Density ratios and supports under the rescaling μ ↦ λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ (supplied proof, step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P and t > 0. Put μ^{y,t} := ofReal(t⁻¹^n)•μ.map(η_{y,t}), where η_{y,t} = dilation y t, η_{y,t}(z) = −t⁻¹y + t⁻¹z = t⁻¹(z − y). Then for every w ∈ ℝ^P: (a) limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρ^n) = limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(B_ρ(y + tw))/(ω_nρ^n) (limsups in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>]0, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, ENNReal division by ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)); and (b) μ^{y,t}(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0 if and only if μ(B_ε(y + tw)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → (∀ w : Euclid P, limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => (ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) • μ.map (dilation y t)) (ball w ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) = limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => μ (ball (y + t • w) ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ ∀ w : Euclid P, (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → (ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) • μ.map (dilation y t)) (ball w ε) ≠ 0) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ (ball (y + t • w) ε) ≠ 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 3 of that proof ("Rescaling, any measure μ").
1. (The map.) Unfolding dilation and dilationCLM, η(z) := dilation y t z = −(t⁻¹•y) + t⁻¹•z = t⁻¹•(z − y). η is affine and continuous, hence Borel measurable.
2. (Preimages of balls.) For w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ: t⁻¹(z − y) − w = t⁻¹(z − (y + tw)) and |t⁻¹v| = t⁻¹|v| (t > 0). Hence η(z) ∈ B_ρ(w) ⟺ t⁻¹|z − (y + tw)| < ρ ⟺ |z − (y + tw)| < tρ. So η⁻¹(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(y + tw).
3. (Ball formula.) Open balls are Borel, so Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (η measurable) give μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w)) = ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·μ(η⁻¹(B_ρ(w))) = ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{tρ}(y + tw)) for all ρ.
4. (Ratio identity for ρ > 0.) Let k := ofReal(t^n). Since t^n > 0, k ∈ (0, ∞) and ofReal(t⁻¹^n) = ofReal((t^n)⁻¹) = k⁻¹ (inv_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos). Also ofReal((tρ)^n) = ofReal(t^n·ρ^n) = k·ofReal(ρ^n) (mul_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_mul with t^n ≥ 0). Put b := ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n). Here ω_n ∈ (0, ∞): it is the Haar volume of the nonempty, open, bounded unit ball of Euclid n. With ρ^n > 0 this gives b ∈ (0, ∞). Let a := μ(B_{tρ}(y + tw)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Then μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w))/b = k⁻¹·a·b⁻¹ = a·(k·b)⁻¹ by ENNReal.mul_inv (k ≠ 0, k ≠ ∞, b ≠ 0, b ≠ ∞). Since ω_n·ofReal((tρ)^n) = k·b, this equals a/(ω_n·ofReal((tρ)^n)). Thus, with H(r) := μ(B_r(y + tw))/(ω_n·ofReal(r^n)), the two functions ρ ↦ μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) and ρ ↦ H(tρ) agree for every ρ > 0. The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>]0, so the two functions have the same limsup along 𝓝[>]0 (Filter.limsup_congr with eventually_nhdsWithin_of_forall).
5. (Change of variables in the limsup.) Let m(ρ) := tρ. m maps (0, ∞) onto (0, ∞) with inverse r ↦ r/t, and both maps are continuous at 0 with value 0. So Tendsto m (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝[>]0) and Tendsto (r ↦ r/t) (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝[>]0). Hence map m (𝓝[>]0) ≤ 𝓝[>]0 and 𝓝[>]0 = map m (map (r ↦ r/t) 𝓝[>]0) ≤ map m 𝓝[>]0, i.e. map m (𝓝[>]0) = 𝓝[>]0. Since limsup u f = limsSup (map u f) and map (H∘m) f = map H (map m f), we get limsup_{𝓝[>]0}(H∘m) = limsup_{map m 𝓝[>]0} H = limsup_{𝓝[>]0} H. In Mathlib, comap_mulLeft_nhdsGT_zero with Filter.map_comap_of_surjective (mul_left_surjective₀) gives map (t * ·) 𝓝[>]0 = 𝓝[>]0, and Filter.limsup_comp rewrites the limsup. Together with step 4 this proves (a).
6. (Supports, (b).) By step 3, for every ε > 0, μ^{y,t}(B_ε(w)) = ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·μ(B_{tε}(y + tw)). The factor ofReal(t⁻¹^n) is nonzero because t⁻¹^n > 0, so μ^{y,t}(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 ⟺ μ(B_{tε}(y + tw)) ≠ 0 (mul_ne_zero_iff). (⇐) Given ε > 0, apply the hypothesis at radius tε > 0. (⇒) Given δ > 0, apply the hypothesis at ε := δ/t > 0, for which tε = δ. ∎
proof_key_steps: η_{y,t}⁻¹(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(y + tw), so μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w)) = t^{−n}μ(B_{tρ}(y + tw)).
For ρ > 0 the density ratio of μ^{y,t} at (w, ρ) equals that of μ at (y + tw, tρ) (ENNReal arithmetic with finite nonzero factors).
ρ ↦ tρ maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0, so the limsups agree.
t^{−n} ≠ 0 and ε ↦ tε is a bijection of (0, ∞), so the support conditions agree.
